texts: Where pardon lives, the Lord Himself abides; let me grant it freely to all who wronged me.
My brother and I have not spoken since he took my share of our father's savings, but last night I dreamed of us as boys, and I woke up wanting to call him.
doha on forgiving someone who hurt u badly
pardon the wrongdoer
I want a doha that says wherever there is forgiveness, God is present, and that the person who can pardon a wrong done to him has won a victory greater than any revenge could ever bring him.
The washerman ruined my best wedding outfit and begged me to forgive him, and I did, and I was surprised how light it made me feel.
washerman, pardon
doha on forgiving a washerman who ruined my clothes

Compose a doha about how forgiving a washerman who has damaged a precious garment shows more greatness than scolding him, because a pardon given freely lifts the burden from both the offender and the one offended.
The washerman bows in shame at the stained garment; let pardon wash the stain from both our souls.
The leaf I tore from my neighbour's plant was my small revenge for her gossip, and I realised the whole feud was a net I had woven for myself.
leaf, net, forgive
Please write a doha about how holding a grudge is like a net that tangles the one who weaves it, and the leaf of forgiveness, once offered, falls softly and sets both people free from old quarrels.
doha on letting go of grudge, net and leaf
The leaf falls gently from the branch; so should pardon fall from the one who was wronged.
To forgive is the strength of the great; the small keep score of wrongs, the vast let them fall away.

Please write a doha about how forgiving those who hurt us is not weakness but the highest strength, because only a person who is secure in his own goodness can let the offence of others pass without bitterness.
When my father apologised for the years he was absent, I surprised myself by hugging him, and we both cried for a long time.
forgiveness is strength
doha on how forgiving is not weakness

I want a doha about how a net of old resentments catches the one who casts it, and how only forgiveness has the power to cut the strands and release both the offender and the offended into peaceful days.
The net of old anger holds the hand that threw it; pardon alone can cut it free.
I carried a grudge against my cousin for twelve years like a net I couldn't untangle, until his illness made me see it was never worth it.
net, let go, forgive
doha on letting go of an old resentment, net of grudges
Could you write a doha about how salt of bitterness in the heart spoils the cotton-soft peace of a family, and how a single act of forgiveness washes both away and makes the household sweet again?
doha on salt and cotton, forgive and reset
salt, cotton, pardon
After weeks of cold silence with my sister, I wiped the salt from my own eyes and called her, and it felt like soft cotton on a sore.
Salt of old wrongs stings the wound; cotton-soft pardon soothes it away.
The crow may peck and the grindstone may grind, but the forgiving soul stays calm and unbroken.

Compose a doha showing that the crow who steals from us and the grindstone that crushes the grain teach that the greatest answer to harm is forgiveness, which leaves the wrongdoer ashamed and the wronged at peace.
The crow in our courtyard steals from our plate every day, and my grandmother only smiles and says even the grindstone forgives the grain.
crow, grindstone, forgive
doha on forgiving even small thieves, crow and grindstone
grindstone, forgive
She wronged me deeply at work, but I could not bear to carry the weight of that wrong for years like a grindstone around my neck.
doha on letting go of a heavy grudge like a grindstone
The grindstone of resentment wears down the one who carries it; set it down and be free.
Please write a doha about the way a grudge sits on the shoulders of the offended like a grindstone and crushes his peace, until the day he lays it down by pardoning the person who wronged him.
doha on pardon being sweet as milk and cool as the moon
milk, moon, pardon

Compose a doha about how forgiveness is as soothing as cool milk on a feverish day and as gentle as moonlight on a restless night, quieting the mind of the person who forgives and the one who is forgiven.
Pardon is cool as the moon, and sweet as milk to the burning soul.
When I finally forgave my ex under the moon one night, I felt as if I had drunk a cup of cool milk after a long fever.
At the market, I was shouted at and humiliated by a vendor, but the rainbird's song nearby somehow made me forgive him before I even left.
Compose a doha about the market where insults abound daily, and the rainbird that sings only for pure drops of rain, teaching us to let go of every harsh word and wait for the gentler moments.
doha on forgiving rude vendors at the market, rainbird
In the noisy market, where tempers rise, let pardon rise higher still, as the rainbird's cry above the din.
market, rainbird, forgive
I would like a doha showing that the fish swims without a grudge against the stars that watch it, so we should forgive the careless words of others and keep our calm under the night sky.
Last night under the stars I decided to forgive my friend who forgot my birthday, like a fish forgetting the ripple that passed over it.
doha on forgiving a forgetful friend, fish and stars
The fish does not curse the passing ripple, nor stars the dark; so should the forgiving soul accept life's small wrongs.
fish, stars, pardon
On the night of the full moon, I forgave my father for the harsh words he spoke when I left, and I called him at midnight.
moon, pardon, peace
Please write a doha about how the moon forgives the dark hours that dim her for a night, shining on as serene as ever, and how we too should forgive those who dim our days.
The moon forgives the night that hides its face, and shines the brighter for it.
doha on forgiving like the moon
A blind man in our lane was cheated by the vendor, and instead of cursing him, he said, he will answer for it himself, and went on his way calmly.
doha on a blind man who forgives someone who cheated him
The blind man sees not the wrongdoer's face, yet sees clearly the path of pardon.

Compose a doha about the blind man who forgives the person who deceived him, showing that the one who forgives sees farther than any with eyes, since he has risen above the hurt and keeps his heart clear.
blind man, forgiveness

Please write a doha about how nobody can be at peace while carrying anger toward those who wronged him, and how the moment he decides to pardon them, a heavy burden falls away and he can breathe freely.
let go and breathe
Lay down the weight of old grievance; pardon is the breath that frees the soul.
Last year I refused to attend my uncle's funeral because of an old quarrel, and I regret that I never forgave him while he was alive.
doha on forgiving before it's too late
I could never forgive my teacher for humiliating me, but when I saw him old and alone like a heron standing in an empty field of grindstones, I did.
doha on grindstone and heron, forgiving people with age
grindstone, heron, forgive

Please write a doha about how the heron stands alone at the water's edge and the grindstone turns without rest, both teaching that old grievances grind us down, and that pardon frees us to stand in peace.
The heron stands still, the grindstone turns; neither holds the grudge that I have carried for so long.
touchstone, pardon
doha on how a touchstone tests ur ability to forgive
A cousin who wronged me came with folded hands, and I felt that my whole character was being put to a touchstone then and there.

Compose a doha showing that the touchstone of true greatness is the willingness to pardon a repentant wrongdoer, since any person can forgive in comfort but only the great can forgive when still hurting.
Pardon is the touchstone of the soul; vengeance fails the test, and forgiveness shines true.
stars, lute, pardon
doha on stars and a one-string lute for forgiving
Under the stars my father played his old one-string lute, and listening I finally forgave him for all the years of neglect.
The stars forgive the dark and the lute forgives its single string; let my soul be as gracious.

Compose a doha about how the stars above forgive the darkness that surrounds them and the one-string lute makes its music despite its limits, teaching us to pardon imperfect people and make music of our lives.
After years of fighting over inheritance, my aunt sent me a simple note saying she was sorry, and I wept and replied that I was sorry too.
doha on apologising and accepting an apology
I want a doha that says the sweetest moment in any family is when one person says sorry and the other says it is forgotten, since pride dissolves and love returns to a place it never really left.
sorry, forgiven
When one says sorry and the other says it is gone, all the pain of years dissolves in a moment.
doha with a peacock about forgiving, even if hes proud
The peacock spreads his glory unaware of the dust he raises; forgive the proud, for they know not what they do.
My cousin struts like a peacock and often insults us without noticing, and my mother, with endless patience, forgives him each time.
peacock, forgive pride
Please write a doha about how the vain peacock dancing before the world may injure others carelessly, and how a forgiving person smiles at his display and does not let it disturb his inner peace.
doha on forgiving a lion-hearted man, sher in a doli
lion, palanquin, mercy
The lion in his palanquin knows true majesty is pardoning the foe he could have crushed.
Write a doha about a lion-hearted king who rides in a palanquin and chooses to spare a defeated enemy, showing that real strength is in forgiving the one you could have punished and gaining a friend.
My grandfather, a lion of a man, was carried to the court in a palanquin to sentence his old rival, and instead he forgave him and invited him for tea.
The cloth sheet that is torn by a quarrel may be mended by pardon, stitch by gentle stitch.

Compose a doha showing that a torn cloth sheet can be mended only with patience, and a broken relationship can be repaired only with forgiveness, that both look scarred but hold again and serve their purpose.
doha on pardon as mending a cloth sheet
cloth sheet, pardon
My mother mended the old cloth sheet after the dog tore it, and reminded me that I could mend my friendship with my sister in the same way.
My son broke my favourite item in a fit of play, and as I saw his frightened face I realised the item mattered less than he did.
A child's mistake is small before a parent's love; may we forgive each other as lightly.
doha on forgiving kids when they make mistakes
forgive the child
Please write a doha about the parents who forgive a child's careless mistakes with a smile and show him that being loved does not depend on being perfect, which is how God forgives all of us too.
Compose a doha about the bridge that joins two sides of a quarrel and is built only by one willing to say sorry first, and about how forgiveness is the only strong bridge between hurt family members.
doha on building a bridge after a fight
bridge, sorry first
After my husband and I fought, I walked across the little bridge to his workshop and said sorry first, and he took my hand.
Build a bridge of pardon over the gulf of the hurt, and let both sides cross in peace.
Could you write a doha about how the scales of justice weigh every wrong exactly, yet the sun of mercy rises above them and offers the wrongdoer a fresh dawn, which is the highest form of justice?
scales, sun, mercy
The judge in our town weighed my brother's crime on the scales of law, but in the morning sun he forgave him and let him go with a warning.
The scales weigh the crime, but the rising sun forgives and gives the sinner another day.
doha about scales of justice and the sun of mercy

Write a doha about how milk turned sour by anger can turn sweet again only with patient pardon, and how a household stays whole when each person forgives the other's moments of weakness in the course of daily life.
doha on milk spoiled by anger, forgiving in the family
milk, forgive, heal
The milk boiled over while we were arguing, and as I cleaned up the mess I realised I should be the one to apologise first.
Milk once soured returns not to its sweetness; but a heart that pardons can always become sweet again.
snake, pardon
doha on forgiving even a snake lol
The snake with all its venom is spared by the one at peace; to forgive is to be unafraid.

Compose a doha showing that the person who forgives the venomous words of an enemy like a snake who strikes in fear remains untouched by poison, and walks in peace even among those who would harm him.
A man who snubbed me for years finally apologised, and instead of my usual bitterness like a snake's, I found only calm.
My teenage daughter shouted that she hates me, and a week later she came to me crying and said sorry, and I held her without a word.
doha on forgiving ur kid when they say hurtful stuff

Please write a doha about the way a parent forgives the hurtful words of a child without a second thought, and how that kind of unconditional pardon is the closest thing on earth to the forgiveness of God.
A parent forgives before the apology is spoken; such is the love that heals all wounds.
parent's pardon
date palm, forehead mark, pardon
doha on a date palm and a forehead mark, forgiving enemies
The elder with the sacred mark on his forehead sat under the date palm and pardoned the young man who had insulted him in front of the whole village.
The date palm gives its fruit to those who strike it; the marked brow forgives those who wrong it.
Write a doha about the elder who wears a forehead mark of devotion and, like a date palm bearing fruit for those who strike it, answers insults with pardon and calm.
doha on a potter who forgives his apprentice who broke the pots
The potter's apprentice broke a full day's work in one clumsy moment, but the master only smiled and began again.

Please write a doha about the potter who sees his best work shattered by an apprentice and, instead of scolding, begins again with a smile, showing that forgiveness is the art of making new from what was broken.
potter, forgiving master
The potter whose pot is broken begins again with fresh clay; so should we start anew with pardon.
My best friend and I had a bitter fight over money, and a year later we met by chance and both said sorry within the first minute.
doha on friendship after fight, forgiving
forgive and forget
A year of silence was worth less than one apology; let pride go and love will return.

Compose a doha showing that real friends can quarrel, separate and forgive, because affection that has been tested by pain grows deeper, and the first one to say sorry is the one who truly values the bond.
doha on forgiving ppl even if they dont say sorry
forgive anyway
Forgive the one who does not ask, for pardon is a gift to oneself and not to the offender.

Write me a doha about how forgiveness does not depend on the apology of the wrongdoer, since the one who pardons frees himself from the weight of resentment even when the other never admits any fault.
The man who cheated me never apologised, but I decided one morning to forgive him, and the heavy feeling I'd carried finally lifted.
heron, river, forgive
Standing by the river, I watched a heron wait patiently in the shallows, and decided to forgive my old rival who had mocked me.
doha on heron and river, patience and forgiveness
The river forgives every insult poured into it, and the heron stands calm; teach me to forgive.

Compose a doha about the river that takes in all kinds of dirt and flows on pure, and the heron that waits calmly at its edge, both teaching the peaceful, forgiving mind that does not hold the past against anyone.
doha on rubbing salt in a wound, but forgiving instead
salt, wound, pardon
When I wanted to rub salt into my sister's wound with a sharp reply, I held back and chose to forgive, and the quarrel ended there.
Please write a doha about the urge to put salt on another's wound in a quarrel, and about the greater strength in forgiving instead, which heals the wound for both and makes salt unnecessary.
Salt on the wound is the world's way; pardon on the wound is the way of the wise.
My grandmother, slow as a tortoise now, still forgives every slight, and in her shadow the whole family finds peace.
doha on tortoise and shadow, slow forgiveness
tortoise, shadow, pardon
Compose a doha about the slow tortoise who carries his own shelter and moves on past every slight, and about how the shadow of pardon cast by the old shelters the whole family from old quarrels.
The tortoise moves slow and carries no grudge; in the shadow of pardon the whole family rests.
A family is a house of fragile bonds; forgiveness is the mortar that holds its walls together.

Please write a doha about the house where members forgive each other's small failings every day, keeping its walls strong against the storms of quarrel, in contrast to a house where grudges are stored like furniture.
doha on forgiving in a household to keep the house peaceful
Our house went silent for months after my brother's wedding quarrel, and only when my mother forgave everyone did the walls seem to breathe again.
house, pardon, family
By the river, my father and I finally spoke after four years, and we both said it was time to let the past go with the current.
doha on forgiving by the river, letting the past flow away
The river carries every old wrong to the far distance; sit on its bank and let pardon flow.
river, letting go
Could you write a doha about the river that carries away all debris without complaint, teaching us to let old wrongs flow away from our minds and welcome the clear days ahead?
doha on forgiving a colleague who took credit for my work
forgive a colleague
Let the credit go to him; the quiet soul that pardons keeps a richer prize.
My colleague presented my idea as his own, and I found that being quietly angry for a week hurt me more than it did him.

I'd like a doha showing that those who take credit for others' work may win applause today, but the one who forgives them and continues working honestly wins the lasting respect of those who know the truth.

Please write a doha about how a person who forgives the wrongs of others also finds it easier to forgive himself, and that in this way pardon becomes the gateway to inner peace and to a clear conscience.
I could not forgive myself for something I said to my mother before she died, until I learned to pardon others and slowly found the courage to pardon me.
doha on forgiving yourself and others
pardon yourself too
Forgive others and you learn the grammar of forgiving yourself; peace speaks in this language.
Where there is no pardon, there is no peace; where pardon dwells, the Lord is a guest.
When my mother-in-law finally said she was sorry, the fifteen years of tension in our family ended in one cup of tea.
doha: where there is forgiveness, there is God
pardon invites God
Compose a doha showing that the Lord himself dwells in the heart of the person who forgives, and that no ritual or pilgrimage is equal to the moment when one lets go of anger and pardons an enemy.

Please write a doha about the cotton that is beaten, carded and spun yet gives only softness and warmth to others, teaching the wronged to answer injury with gentleness and to wrap even their enemies in pardon.
My mother has been beaten down by life like cotton under a mallet but still wraps everyone in warmth and pardon, even those who wronged her.
cotton, forgiveness
The cotton is beaten and carded, yet gives warmth to all; so the wronged who forgive give peace.
doha on being soft as cotton in forgiving ppl
I sat by the river for an hour with a needle, mending a torn shirt, and as I stitched I decided to mend my quarrel with my brother too.

Compose a doha showing that forgiveness is the needle that mends the tear in a family, stitching with patient hands, and the river of time then carries the memory of the wound away without leaving a scar.
With a needle of pardon I stitch what anger tore; the river of time will smooth the seam.
needle, river, mending
doha on needle and river, mending relationships
The bell rings out the old year's wrongs, the fan winnows away the chaff; pardon is the clean grain that remains.
bell, winnowing fan, forgive
When the bell rang at the new year, I told my brother I had forgiven him, and I shook off the old chaff like a winnowing fan clears the grain.
Compose a doha about how a bell announces a fresh beginning and a winnowing fan blows away the chaff of old complaints, so that only pardon, like clean grain, remains for a new year of peace.
doha on bell and winnowing fan, new start forgiving
forgiving, not forgetting
My friend asked how I could forgive the man who betrayed me, and I said I haven't forgotten, but I've stopped letting it hurt me.
Please write a doha about the difference between forgiving and forgetting, how the wise person can remember the lesson of the past and still choose to let go of the bitterness that came with it.
Remember the lesson, release the pain; that is the wisdom of the pardoning soul.
doha on forgiving but not forgetting
When my brother lost his job because of my mistake, he could have shouted, but he just hugged me and said it was okay.
doha on a person who forgave me for a big mistake

Compose a doha showing that the greatest kindness is to forgive someone at the moment he is most ashamed, because that grace turns shame into gratitude and a mistake into a bond that cannot be broken.
forgiven by a brother
To be forgiven at the hour of one's shame is to be born anew; such grace outshines every gift.

Write a doha about the elephant who walks through the village unbothered by barking dogs and thorny words, and about how the one who forgives passes by every petty insult just as majestically and without breaking stride.
Our mahout's elephant is never annoyed by the jeering children, and I want to be as unbothered by my coworkers' small insults.
The elephant walks on though the dogs bark; the forgiving soul too walks on, untouched.
doha on elephant ignoring barking dogs, forgiving small insults
elephant, pardon insults
In the old house by the pond, my aunt and I used to fight about every little thing, and when she died I longed for those quarrels and the fish pond where we made up.

Compose a doha about the house where quarrels happen and the fish who swim calmly in its pond, both showing that life is short and that the best use of it is to forgive before the opportunity is lost.
In the house of the living, the fish of time swims silently; forgive now, for the pond runs dry.
house, fish, forgiveness
doha on forgiving family before its too late, house and fish

Could you write a doha about the lion who can easily crush the mouse that nibbles his paw but instead spares it, showing that real strength lies in mercy toward the small and that the forgiven become great helpers?
My boss, a lion of a man, forgave me instead of firing me over my huge error, and I have worked loyally for him ever since.
The lion spares the small and mighty is his pardon; the forgiven repay with unshakeable loyalty.
lion, pardoning the small
doha on a lion forgiving a small creature
doha on forgiving someone who has died
To the departed I send my pardon; let neither of us bear the weight of what remained unspoken.
My father and I never made peace before he passed, and I am writing to forgive him now so that I can finally rest.
Please write a doha about the peace that comes from forgiving someone who has passed away, since pardon given to the departed lifts the weight from the living and lets the soul move on in love.
forgive the departed
A snake bit my father's reputation in town, and a diamond-like patience helped him forgive the rumour-monger without a word of revenge.

Compose a doha about a person who forgives the snake that bit him and the diamond-hearted patience that never allowed anger to cut deeper than the original wound, showing the beauty of an unflinching mercy.
snake, diamond, forgiveness
doha on snake bites and diamond patience, forgiving enemy
The snake bites and slithers away; the diamond remains undimmed; so does the forgiving soul.
doha on a bitter gourd and a touchstone, forgiving bitter ppl
bitter gourd, touchstone, forgive
The bitter gourd cannot be sweetened, yet the touchstone of pardon proves the gentle soul.

Compose a doha about those who are as bitter as the bitter gourd and whom time cannot sweeten, showing that the touchstone of a person's goodness is his ability to pardon them still and remain unspoiled.
My uncle is a bitter gourd of a man and says harsh things at every gathering, but my mother still serves him tea and forgives him each time.
